name: The cutter
tagline: Carves the car body out of the legal block, one safe cut at a time.
what: Starts from the full block of material the rules allow, with every rule zone already marked.

Moves the surface in or out wherever it is told, in small steps, and checks every rule after each step: required solid areas, required open areas, left-right symmetry, one single piece, and a shape a real milling machine can cut.
Re-sizes the whole body after each cut so the car always weighs the target.
Hands over a clean, closed 3D shape. It never decides what is faster; it only cuts safely.

items.name: Older body: random cars tested (1 square = 10 cars)

now: Grid weight gap fixed. Two causes found and removed: the mill skipped its corner cut when the body stood just back from a keep-clear corner, and a piece hanging on by a hair was dropped on one grid only. Grid check on 20 bodies: 19 read so far, all between 0.10 and 0.48 % (mark 0.5 %); the last one is still running. Next: weight sizing of 200 bodies and the 200-body carving test on this cutter, then the tag.

log.text: Board created. Waiting for the go to start this phase.
Repository cleaned: unused and outdated files removed. The symmetry test is fixed; one mesh test still fails and is the first job.
Started. A test that switches shape rules off one at a time found the one behind the failing mesh test. Fix comes next.
A closer look showed the cause: a hair-thin strip of material left behind, too thin to turn into a clean surface.
Fixed: hair-thin strips are now cleaned away after every cut. All checks of all five parts pass.
Cutting tool written, with checks for direction, refusals, rules and saving.
Cutting tool finished: all checks of all five parts pass. Parts three and five can use it now.
First weight test of twenty carved bodies: none under the floor, but six were slightly heavy. Looking into it.
Weight sizing fixed for bodies whose weight jumps in steps. Added five hand-checked milling shapes and a finishing step that writes the finished body.
Weight now lands on target for all twenty test bodies. First carving test: all six cars built, but all had too wide a cartridge chamber.
Found why carved cars had too wide a cartridge chamber: the grid put its wall half a step out. The finished body now has the chamber at its exact size.
Same-result test: ten bodies built twice, every file identical.
Grid-size test failed its weight bar on nineteen of twenty bodies. Cause: rule zones are drawn cell by cell. Asked the team lead how to proceed.
Weight proof: one hundred ninety nine of two hundred on target, one light, a failure. Chamber still too wide on every car, a failure. Two thousand car test started; exact rule zones begun.

Causes found: milling snapped the surface to the grid, the weight search gave up too early, and a crack along the centre line widened the chamber. Fixes written; one older check broke and is being traced.
Milling now keeps the drawn surface; grid weight spread fell from up to two percent to under one. Every main rule zone now has an exact edge; checking.
Chamber now the right size and confirmed. Big carving test restarted on the fixed code. All checks pass. Grid weight difference is down to about one percent; still failing its bar.
Part 4's 3 reference cars pass on fef4130. Milling now always on one fixed fine grid, as the team lead decided. Big test starts on the frozen tag.
Chamber agreed with Part 4: the plug gauge passes and the leftover crack is gone. Part 2 found the body jumps between two nearby skin thicknesses; finding the cause.

Found and fixed two causes: the tidy-up of the shape field shrank the body a little each time (the main grid weight gap), and the skin made the front of the body creep into the nose (the sudden shape jump Part 2 saw). Rechecking.

200-body random carving green; same-result test green. Grid weight gap traced to two places (a spot behind the front wheel in the milling step, and the rule-zone trim along the rear). Diagnostic run started to confirm the cause before the cutter is changed.
Grid weight gap fixed in two steps. Grid check on 20 bodies went from up to 1.98 % to 0.48 % at most (19 of 20 read, mark 0.5 %). Unit tests green on the first step, running on the second.
